A prior agent black-box probed the jsonschema behavior family "validator-selection" of the program at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (usage: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'; prints validator class, True/False, top-level error count).

Its findings were:
---
FILE: /workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl (315 lines, JSONL). Each line is {"a": <instance JSON text>, "b": <schema JSON text>, "out": <exact stdout incl. trailing \n>, "exit": <int>} plus, when non-empty, "stderr": <exact stderr> and, for CLI-shape probes, "argv": [...] (the raw argv actually passed; for those the a/b fields are the effective parsed values or null when the run never got that far).

=== 1. $schema -> validator class mapping (validator_for) ===
Exactly six URIs are recognized, and ONLY these exact spellings (each additionally accepted with a single trailing '#'):
  http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema  -> Draft3Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema  -> Draft4Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema  -> Draft6Validator
  http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema  -> Draft7Validator
  https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema -> Draft201909Validator
  https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema -> Draft202012Validator
SCHEME IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Drafts 03/04/06/07 are registered under http ONLY: 'https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' is UNKNOWN -> warning + Draft202012Validator. 2019-09/2020-12 are registered under https ONLY: 'http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' is UNKNOWN -> warning + Draft202012Validator. Trailing '#' is optional and irrelevant for all six (both '...2020-12/schema' and '...2020-12/schema#' work).

Unknown $schema string => one line on STDERR, exactly:
  "test13.py:15: DeprecationWarning: The metaschema specified by $schema was not found. Using the latest draft to validate, but this will raise an error in the future.\n"
and then Draft202012Validator is used. Exit stays 0, stdout unaffected. Tested-unknown values that all fall back with that warning: 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' and 'https://json-schema.org/schema#' and 'http://json-schema.org/schema' (the "latest" alias is NOT registered), draft-00/01/02/05, all hyper-schema URIs (http://json-schema.org/hyper-schema#, .../draft-07/hyper-schema#, .../draft-04/hyper-schema#, https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/hyper-schema, .../2020-12/hyper-schema), vocabulary meta URIs (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/meta/core, .../meta/applicator, .../2019-09/meta/core), a nonexistent draft (2021-12), 'urn:foo', 'foo', '', '   ', '#'.

=== 2. URI normalization: it is urlsplit(uri).geturl(), and the result is a CACHED (hashed) lookup key ===
Observed normalization behavior, which matters a lot:
- Scheme is case-folded to lowercase: 'HTTP://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and 'HtTp://...' -> Draft7Validator. But 'HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' -> ALSO Draft202012Validator, though that is the fallback: it emits the DeprecationWarning (host case matters, see next). Careful: 'HTTPS://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft/2020-12/schema' warns; scheme-only uppercasing of a 2020-12 URI ('HTTPS://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema') ALSO warns in my probe -- see the vector; do not assume symmetry, use the recorded vectors.
- Host case is NOT normalized: 'http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#' and 'http://Json-Schema.org/...' -> unknown/warn. Path case is NOT normalized: '/DRAFT-07/schema#' and '/draft-07/Schema#' -> unknown/warn.
- An EMPTY query is dropped by geturl(): 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema?' -> Draft7Validator (no warning!). Same for 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema?' -> Draft202012Validator with NO warning. A non-empty query is kept: '...schema?x=1' -> warn.
- An empty fragment is dropped, a non-empty one is kept: '...schema#' == '...schema'; but '...schema##' (fragment '#'), '...schema#?' , '...schema#foo', '...schema#/definitions/foo' all -> warn. Same for 2019-09/2020-12 with '##'.
- TAB, CR and LF are stripped from ANYWHERE in the string before parsing: '\thttp://...', '\nhttp://...', '\rhttp://...', 'http\t://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/sch\nema#' ALL resolve to Draft7Validator.
- LEADING spaces are stripped, TRAILING spaces are NOT: ' http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and '  http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema' -> Draft7Validator; 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema# ' and 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema ' and 'https://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema ' -> warn/fallback. (So the underlying urlsplit does lstrip only, not strip.)
- No path normalization: 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/../draft-07/schema#' -> warn. No default-port removal: 'http://json-schema.org:80/draft-07/schema#' -> warn. Missing scheme/authority variants ('//json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#', 'http:/json-schema.org/...', 'http:///json-schema.org/...', 'http://json-schema.org//draft-07/schema#') -> warn.

=== 3. Non-string $schema values: three distinct outcomes ===
The lookup key goes into a functools-cached normalize() that first HASHES the argument, then calls urlsplit, whose _coerce_args treats FALSY non-str as ''.
- $schema: null, false, "" (and "   ", which lstrips to "") => NO crash: normalizes to '' -> not found -> DeprecationWarning + Draft202012Validator, exit 0, "Draft202012Validator/True/0".
- $schema: any truthy number or true (1, -1, 1.5, true) => UNCAUGHT AttributeError: "'int'/'float'/'bool' object has no attribute 'decode'" (urllib/parse.py _decode_args). exit 1, full Python traceback on stderr, no stdout.
- $schema: {} , [] , {"a":1} , ["http://..."] , {"$ref":"x"} => UNCAUGHT TypeError: "unhashable type: 'dict'" / "'list'" raised inside jsonschema/_utils.py normalize (the lru_cache hashing the key). exit 1, traceback, no stdout. NOTE: 0 also crashes? No -- {"$schema":0} FALLS BACK with the warning (0 is falsy), while {"$schema":1} and {"$schema":-1} crash. That asymmetry is real and recorded.
All crash tracebacks end with the PyInstaller line "[PYI-NNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' due to unhandled exception!" (the PYI number varies run to run, so do not diff on it).

=== 4. Whole-schema (the --b document) types ===
- true  -> Draft202012Validator / True / 0 for every instance type tested (1, "s", [1], {"k":1}, null, true, 1.5).
- false -> Draft202012Validator / False / 1 for every instance type.
- {}    -> Draft202012Validator / True / 0.
- null  -> crash in validator_for: TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable (the `"$schema" not in schema` membership test). exit 1.
- number (1, 0, 1.5, -1) -> crash in validator_for: TypeError: argument of type 'int'/'float' is not iterable. exit 1.
- string ("hello", "") and array ([], [1,2], ["a"]) -> validator_for SURVIVES (membership `in` works on str/list) and returns Draft202012Validator, then the crash happens LATER while constructing the validator/resource: AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'get' in referencing/jsonschema.py:_dollar_id. exit 1, no stdout. So the failure point differs by type even though the observable result (exit 1, empty stdout) is the same.

=== 5. $schema is root-only; $id is irrelevant to dispatch ===
A $schema nested inside properties/items/additionalProperties/definitions/allOf does NOT change the chosen validator class (still Draft202012Validator or whatever the root said), and does not suppress or add a warning. Examples: {"properties":{"a":{"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-03/schema#","type":"string"}}} with {"a":1} -> Draft202012Validator/False/1. {"$schema":draft-07, "properties":{"a":{"$schema":2020-12,...}}} -> Draft7Validator. A root with only "$id" or only "id" -> Draft202012Validator/True/0, no warning. $id alongside a valid $schema does not disturb dispatch.

=== 6. Top-level error counting (line 3) ===
Confirmed: is_valid (line 2) and len(list(iter_errors)) (line 3) are consistent -- False iff count>0.
- Sibling keywords each yield their own top-level error: {"type":"string","minimum":5,"maxLength":2} on 1 -> 2 (type + minimum; maxLength is inapplicable to a number).
- properties: one top-level error per failing property, at any depth (they are yielded via descend, not nested): 2 failing props -> 2; 3 -> 3; a single failing grandchild -> 1; two failing grandchildren under one child -> 2.
- items (schema form): one top-level error per failing element: [1,2] -> 2, [1,2,3] -> 3.
- allOf: sub-errors DO surface individually -> {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"boolean"}]} on 1 -> 2.
- anyOf / oneOf / not / if-then: exactly 1 top-level error each (children live in .context).
- $ref: 1 error.
- type as a list: 1 error.
- Combined: {"$schema":X,"properties":{a:string,b:string},"type":"array"} on {"a":1,"b":2} -> 3 in EVERY draft (2 property errors + 1 type error), including under an unknown $schema (which then warns and uses 2020-12).

=== 7. Cross-draft semantics reachable only through correct dispatch ===
- exclusiveMinimum:5 (no minimum) on 3: draft3 True/0, draft4 True/0 (numeric form ignored), draft6/7/2019/2020 False/1.
- minimum:5 + exclusiveMinimum:true on 3: False/1 in ALL six drafts (draft3/4 honour the boolean modifier; 6+ ignore the boolean exclusiveMinimum but minimum:5 alone already fails).
- items as an ARRAY on [1,"a"]: draft3/4/6/7/2019 -> False/1. Draft 2020-12 -> UNCAUGHT AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' (jsonschema/_keywords.py items -> validators.descend -> referencing in_subresource -> _dollar_id), exit 1, traceback. 2020-12 assumes items is a schema and blows up on the list.
- prefixItems on [1,"a"]: ignored (True/0) in draft3/4/6/7/2019; only 2020-12 -> False/1.
- $ref with sibling keywords ({"$ref":"#/definitions/x","definitions":{...},"maximum":1} on 5): draft3/4/6/7 -> 1 error ($ref replaces siblings); 2019-09/2020-12 -> 2 errors (siblings apply).
- const:2 on 1: draft3/4 True/0 (unknown keyword); draft6+ False/1.
- contains on [1]: draft3/4 True/0; draft6+ False/1.
- dependencies:{"a":["b"]} on {"a":1}: draft3/4/6/7 False/1; 2019-09 and 2020-12 True/0 (dependencies removed).
- required:["b"] array form: draft3 ignores it (only 1 error from properties); draft4+ -> 2.
- required:true inside a property subschema: 1 error in every draft (draft3 honours it as "must be present" and it IS present, so only the type error).
- type:"integer" on 1.0: draft3/4 False/1 (float rejected); draft6+ True/0 (1.0 is an integer by value).
- type:"any": VALID (True/0) only in draft3. In draft4/6/7/2019/2020 it raises UNCAUGHT jsonschema.exceptions.UnknownType: "Unknown type 'any' for validator with schema: ..." -> exit 1, traceback that includes the pretty-printed schema and "While checking instance:". Note this crash happens inside is_valid (line 18 of the script), i.e. AFTER the class name would have been computed but BEFORE anything is printed, so stdout is empty.
- $defs vs definitions: both are just plain objects, $ref by JSON pointer works into either in every draft (False/1 each).

=== 8. JSON parsing of the args (before any jsonschema work) ===
--a is json.loads'd first (script line 11), then --b (line 12). Bad JSON -> uncaught json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1, no stdout. Exact messages observed: '' or 'nan' or "'1'" -> "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"; '{' -> "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)"; '01' -> "Extra data: line 1 column 2 (char 1)". Python's json ACCEPTS 'NaN' and 'Infinity' (both -> Draft202012Validator/True/0 against {}), and tolerates leading/trailing whitespace ('1 ', ' 1'). Because --a is parsed before --b, an invalid --a masks an invalid --b.

=== 9. CLI / argparse (prog name is "test13_executable") ===
- Both --a and --b are required=True, type=str. '--a=VAL' and '--a VAL' are both accepted; order is free ('--b {} --a 1' works).
- Repeated options: LAST WINS. '--a 1 --a "x" --b {"type":"string"}' -> True (uses "x"); '--a 1 --b {} --b false' -> False/1 (uses false).
- Missing args, exit 2, stdout empty, stderr exactly:
    "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\ntest13_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a, --b\n"
  (with "--a" or "--b" alone when only one is missing).
- Unknown option / stray positional, exit 2, stderr "usage: ...\ntest13_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: --c 1\n" (or "5", or "extra", or "--"). IMPORTANT: the required-arguments check fires BEFORE the unrecognized check, so '-a 1 -b {}' reports "the following arguments are required: --a, --b" (NOT "unrecognized"), and '-a 1 --b {}' reports "required: --a". Single-dash '-a'/'-b' are NOT accepted (only '--a'/'--b' were registered).
- Uppercase '--A 1 --B {}' -> required-args error (case sensitive).
- '-h' and '--help' print to STDOUT, exit 0, exactly:
    "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A       instance (JSON string)\n  --b B       schema (JSON string)\n"
  ("options:" -- Python 3.10+ wording, not "optional arguments:"). Help wins even when placed after valid --a/--b, and even when --a/--b are absent.
- Prefix abbreviation IS enabled: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all print help (exit 0). '--hell' is not a prefix -> exit 2 required-args error.
- Missing value: '--a --b {}' -> exit 2, "test13_executable: error: argument --a: expected one argument". Same for '--a 1 --b'. A value that looks like an option is rejected the same way: '--a -x' and '--a --1' -> "expected one argument". BUT a negative NUMBER is accepted as a value: '--a -5 --b {}' -> parses -5 fine (argparse's negative-number heuristic, since no option string looks like a negative number). '--a=--b --b={}' is accepted by argparse (the '=' form takes anything) and then fails in json.loads with exit 1.
- Empty-string values: '--a "" --b {}' and '--a= --b=' -> exit 1 JSONDecodeError (argparse accepts them).
- '--' separator: '-- --a 1 --b {}' -> everything after '--' becomes positionals, so exit 2 "required: --a, --b". '--a 1 -- --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --b". '--a 1 --b {} --' -> exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --". Bare '--', '-', '-x' with no other args -> exit 2 required-args error.

=== 10. Exit codes summary ===
0 = normal (3 lines of stdout; a DeprecationWarning may also be on stderr). 1 = uncaught Python exception (traceback on stderr, stdout EMPTY -- nothing is printed partially, since all three prints come after validation). 2 = argparse usage error (usage+error on stderr, stdout empty, except -h/--help which is exit 0 with help on stdout).
---
Gotchas it listed: ["Scheme is NOT interchangeable per draft: drafts 03/04/06/07 are only registered under http://, and 2019-09/2020-12 only under https://. 'https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#' and 'http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema' both fall back to Draft202012Validator WITH the deprecation warning.","The trailing '#' is optional for all six URIs, but an empty QUERY is also dropped: 'http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema?' resolves to Draft7Validator with no warning. '...schema##' and '...schema#?' do NOT resolve.","Normalization is urlsplit(uri).geturl(): scheme lowercased, tab/CR/LF removed from anywhere in the string, LEADING whitespace stripped but TRAILING whitespace NOT. Host and path case are preserved, so 'http://JSON-SCHEMA.ORG/draft-07/schema#' is unknown.","$schema: null, false, \"\" and 0 quietly FALL BACK (warning + 2020-12) because they are falsy and coerce to ''. $schema: 1, -1, 1.5, true CRASH with AttributeError ('no attribute decode'), and $schema: {} or [] CRASH with TypeError: unhashable type. Same 'wrong type' category, three different outcomes.","There is no 'latest' alias: 'http://json-schema.org/schema#' is UNKNOWN and warns. Hyper-schema and per-vocabulary meta URIs (.../meta/core etc.) are also unknown.","A whole-schema of null or a number crashes inside validator_for (TypeError: argument of type X is not iterable), but a whole-schema that is a string or an array survives validator_for (prints nothing anyway) and crashes later in referencing._dollar_id with AttributeError: 'str'/'list' object has no attribute 'get'. All are exit 1 with empty stdout.","$schema is honoured ONLY at the document root. A $schema inside properties/items/definitions/allOf changes nothing and produces no warning.","items given as an ARRAY under $schema 2020-12 is not merely ignored -- it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'), exit 1. Under 2019-09 and earlier it works as tuple validation.","type:\"any\" is valid only in draft-03; in draft-04 and later it raises UnknownType and the process exits 1 with EMPTY stdout (the crash is inside is_valid, before any print).","Error counting: properties/items yield one top-level error per failing child at any nesting depth, and allOf yields one per failing branch, but anyOf/oneOf/not/if-then always yield exactly 1 (children are in .context).","$ref with sibling keywords yields 1 error in drafts 3/4/6/7 ($ref replaces siblings) but 2 in 2019-09/2020-12.","argparse reports missing REQUIRED arguments before unrecognized ones, so '-a 1 -b {}' produces 'the following arguments are required: --a, --b', not an 'unrecognized arguments' message.","Prefix abbreviation is on: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all trigger help (exit 0, help on stdout). Help wins even when --a/--b are also present.","Repeated --a/--b: last occurrence wins, no error.","'--a -5' is accepted (argparse negative-number heuristic) but '--a -x' errors with 'expected one argument'; '--a=--b' is accepted by argparse and only fails later in json.loads.","The help/usage text says 'options:' (Python 3.10+), the prog name is 'test13_executable', and help goes to stdout with exit 0 while usage errors go to stderr with exit 2.","Crash tracebacks end with a PyInstaller line '[PYI-<random>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test13' ...' whose number changes every run -- never diff on it.","--a is json.loads'd before --b, so a malformed instance masks a malformed schema; Python's json accepts NaN/Infinity and surrounding whitespace but rejects 'nan', \"'1'\", and '01'."]
Its vectors are in /workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl (315 lines of JSONL, each {"a","b","out","exit"}).

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Its assignment was:
validator_for / $schema dispatch and top-level plumbing.
Probe: $schema with and without trailing '#'; http vs https scheme for every draft; draft-2019-09/2020-12 with '#'; $schema as a non-string (number, object, array, null, bool) — does it crash or fall back?; schema that is a JSON array; schema that is a string; schema that is a number (known: TypeError crash); schema that is null; $schema pointing at a meta-schema URI with extra path; case sensitivity of the URI; $schema nested inside a subschema (does it change the validator?); empty schema {}; schema with only $id.
Also probe CLI/argparse behavior exhaustively: '--a=VAL' form, '--b=VAL', argument order swapped, repeated '--a' (last wins?), missing one/both args (exit code + exact stderr text), '-h'/'--help' exact stdout, unknown option '--c' (exit code + stderr), a bare positional argument, '--' separator, empty string values, prefix abbreviation (does '--' plus a unique prefix work — try nothing shorter exists since names are 1 char; try '--a' vs '-a' single dash — argparse allows single-dash long options? test '-a 1 -b 1'), and values that look like options (e.g. --a '-5'). Record exact stderr text for errors too (capture stderr into the "out" field for these, and note it in findings).

Your job: find what is MISSING or WRONG. Specifically:
1. Read /workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl (use head/wc/grep, don't dump the whole thing) and check which parts of the assignment were actually probed.
2. Identify untested edges, especially anything affecting ERROR COUNTS or cross-draft differences, and anything a JavaScript reimplementer would get wrong (unicode string length with astral chars, Python regex vs JS regex, float precision, integer vs bool, object key ordering, deep equality of numbers 1 vs 1.0, -0).
3. RUN those missing probes yourself against the executable and APPEND them as JSONL lines to the SAME file /workspace/probes/validator-selection.jsonl (same format: {"a","b","out","exit"}). Use a node script with execFileSync to append so escaping is exact. Never hand-write expected output.
4. Verify a random sample of ~8 existing lines by re-running them and comparing to the recorded "out" — report any mismatch (a mismatch means the file is corrupt/hand-written).

Return: family name, MERGED and CORRECTED findings prose (restate the full spec for this family incorporating both the prior findings and everything new you learned — the implementer reads ONLY your version, so it must be self-contained and complete), the vector file path, the TOTAL line count after your appends (wc -l), and a gotchas list.

=== 8. Types, equality and numbers (the biggest JS-reimplementation traps) ===
- Booleans are NOT numbers here: {"type":"integer"} on true -> False/1 in all six drafts; {"type":"number"} on true -> False/1; {"type":"boolean"} on 1 -> False/1. (jsonschema explicitly excludes bool from the int/number type checks even though Python bool subclasses int.)
- Numeric equality for const/enum is by VALUE across int/float: const 1 accepts instance 1.0 and const 1.0 accepts instance 1 (True/0 in all drafts). enum [1] accepts 1.0.
- -0 equals 0: const 0 accepts -0.0 and const -0.0 accepts 0; enum [0] accepts -0.0. multipleOf 2 on -0.0 -> True/0.
- But bool vs number is NOT equal for const/enum: const 1 on true -> d6+ False/1 (d3/4 True/0 because const is unknown there); const true on 1 -> d6+ False/1; enum [true] on 1 -> False/1; enum [1] on true -> False/1.
- uniqueItems uses the same value equality: [1,1.0] -> DUPLICATE (False/1); [[1,2],[1,2]] -> duplicate; [{"a":1,"b":2},{"b":2,"a":1}] -> duplicate (object key ORDER is irrelevant). But [true,1] -> unique (True/0) and [0,false] -> unique. [1,2,3] -> True/0. [NaN,NaN] -> duplicate (False/1).
- Big integers keep full Python precision: instance 10000000000000000001 with const 10000000000000000001 -> True/0, with const 10000000000000000000 -> False/1 (a JS Number would collapse both to the same double), and {"type":"integer"} accepts it.
- json.loads accepts NaN, Infinity, -Infinity: NaN passes {"type":"number"} (True/0); NaN fails {"const":null} and {"enum":[1]}; Infinity fails {"multipleOf":2} (False/1). 1e400 parses to inf, passes {"type":"number"}, and fails {"maximum":1e308}.
- multipleOf uses Python float division semantics: 4.5 % 1.5 -> True/0; 7.5 with multipleOf 0.1 -> True/0; 0.0075 with multipleOf 0.0001 -> True/0; 1 with multipleOf 0.0001 -> True/0; 1e308 with multipleOf 0.1 -> False/1 (d4+; d3 ignores multipleOf).

=== 9. Strings: length is CODE POINTS, regex is Python `re` ===
- maxLength/minLength count Unicode CODE POINTS, not UTF-16 units. "😀" (one astral emoji) has length 1: {"maxLength":1} -> True/0, {"minLength":2} -> False/1. Two emoji with {"maxLength":2} -> True/0. A JS `.length` implementation would get all three wrong. Combining sequences are NOT normalized: "é" has length 2 ({"maxLength":1} -> False/1) while precomposed "é" has length 1 (True/0). "�" is a normal 1-char string.
- pattern uses Python re.search (UNANCHORED): pattern "b" matches "abc" -> True/0.
- Python `\d`/`\w` are UNICODE-aware by default: pattern "^\\d$" matches "٣" (Arabic-Indic three) -> True/0, while "a" -> False/1. pattern "^\\w$" matches both "_" and "é". JS /\d/ and /\w/ are ASCII-only — this WILL diverge.
- Python `$` matches before a trailing newline: pattern "^a$" on "a\n" -> True/0 (JS would say no match). "^a\\Z" on "a\n" -> False/1. "^a$" on "a\nb" and on "b\na" -> False/1 (no re.MULTILINE).
- Python-only regex syntax is accepted: inline flags "(?i)a" matches "A" -> True/0; named group "(?P<n>x)" works. JS-only syntax is rejected: "(?<n>x)" -> UNCAUGHT re.error "unknown extension ?<n at position 1", exit 1. An invalid pattern like "[" -> UNCAUGHT re.error "unterminated character set at position 0", exit 1. These crashes happen in every draft.
- "format" is NEVER asserted (no format checker is passed): {"format":"email"} on "nope", {"format":"date-time"} on "nope", {"format":"regex"} on "nope" all -> True/0 in every draft.

=== 10. $ref / referencing behavior ===
- Unresolvable JSON pointer: exit 1, "jsonschema.exceptions._WrappedReferencingError: PointerToNowhere: '/definitions/missing' does not exist within {…the whole schema repr…}". Same in all six drafts.
- Any remote or relative $ref that isn't in the schema: exit 1, "_WrappedReferencingError: Unresolvable: http://example.com/nope" (or "Unresolvable: nonexistent.json"). Nothing is fetched from the network or disk.
- {"$ref":"#"} (self-reference to the root) -> exit 1 RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded, in all six drafts.
- Plain-name fragment via {"$id":"#frag"}: works ONLY in draft6 and draft7 (False/1). In d3/d4 and in 2019-09/2020-12 it is exit 1 "_WrappedReferencingError: NoSuchAnchor: 'frag' does not exist within {…}" (2019+ require $anchor; 3/4 use "id").

=== 11. Miscellaneous validation shape ===
- Boolean SUBSCHEMAS work in every draft at the properties level: {"properties":{"a":false}} on {"a":1} -> False/1 in all six; on {} -> True/0. additionalProperties:true -> True/0. (Only boolean `items` crashes in d3/d4.)

- Unknown keywords ($comment, "unknownKw", "x") are always ignored.
- oneOf with TWO matching branches -> False/1 in d4+ (True/0 in d3, no oneOf). anyOf with no match -> False/1 in d4+.

=== 12. JSON parsing of the args ===
--a is json.loads'd FIRST (line 11), then --b (line 12), so a malformed instance masks a malformed schema. Bad JSON -> uncaught json.decoder.JSONDecodeError, exit 1, stdout empty. Exact messages: '' / 'nan' / "'1'" / '-.5' / '-' -> "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"; '{' -> "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 2 (char 1)"; '01' -> "Extra data: line 1 column 2 (char 1)". Python's json ACCEPTS NaN / Infinity / -Infinity and tolerates surrounding whitespace and trailing newlines.

=== 13. CLI / argparse (prog name "test13_executable") ===
- --a and --b are required=True, type=str. '--a=VAL' and '--a VAL' both work; order is free.
- Repeated options: LAST WINS, no error ('--a 1 --a "x"' uses "x"; '--a 1 --b {} --b false' -> False/1; '--a 1 --b {} --a 2' uses 2).
- Values may contain spaces, newlines and non-ASCII UTF-8; all pass through untouched.
- Missing args: exit 2, stdout empty, stderr exactly "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\ntest13_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --a, --b\n" (with only "--a" or only "--b" when just one is missing).
- Unknown option / stray positional: exit 2, "…error: unrecognized arguments: --c 1" (or "extra", "5", "--"). The REQUIRED-argument check fires BEFORE the unrecognized check, so '-a 1 -b {}' reports "the following arguments are required: --a, --b" and '-a 1 --b {}' reports "required: --a". Single-dash '-a'/'-b' are not registered. Uppercase '--A/--B' -> required-args error.
- '-h'/'--help' go to STDOUT with exit 0, exactly: "usage: test13_executable [-h] --a A --b B\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --a A       instance (JSON string)\n  --b B       schema (JSON string)\n" (Python 3.10+ "options:" wording). Help wins even when --a/--b are present and even when placed last.
- Prefix abbreviation is ON: '--h', '--he', '--hel' all print help (exit 0); '--hell' is not a prefix -> exit 2 required-args error.
- Missing value: '--a --b {}' and '--a 1 --b' -> exit 2 "…error: argument --a: expected one argument". Values that look like options are rejected the same way: '--a -x', '--a --1', '--a -Infinity', '--a -1e5'. BUT argparse's negative-number heuristic accepts values matching a plain decimal: '--a -5', '--a -0' (both parse fine, -0 -> Draft202012Validator/True/0) and '--a -.5' (accepted by argparse, then fails in json.loads with exit 1). The '=' form bypasses the heuristic entirely: '--a=-Infinity --b={}' parses to -inf and prints Draft202012Validator/True/0; '--a=--b --b={}' is accepted by argparse and fails later in json.loads.
- Empty-string values: '--a "" --b {}' and '--a= --b=' -> exit 1 JSONDecodeError.
- '--' separator: '-- --a 1 --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --a, --b"; '--a 1 -- --b {}' -> exit 2 "required: --b"; '--a 1 --b {} --' -> exit 2 "unrecognized arguments: --"; bare '--', '-', '-x' alone -> exit 2 required-args error.

=== 14. Exit codes ===
0 = normal (exactly 3 stdout lines; a DeprecationWarning may accompany on stderr), or -h/--help. 1 = uncaught Python exception (traceback on stderr, stdout EMPTY — all three prints come after validation). 2 = argparse usage error (usage + error on stderr, stdout empty).
